questions.q: What are the four sections this lesson says a capstone write-up should reuse from Lesson 33's report structure?
options: Introduction, literature review, conclusion, references
Method, reproduction, extension, limitations
Abstract, results, discussion, acknowledgments
Problem, solution, demo, Q&A
questions.explain: The write-up is structured around method, reproduction, extension, and limitations — a direct application of the technical report structure from Lesson 33 to the capstone's own content.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say "I reproduced the paper" should be turned into a demonstrated claim rather than left as an assertion?
options: Because assertions are against the LTV Academy honor code
Because a comparison table, the claimed tier, and a link to the tracked run let a reader verify the claim rather than take it on faith
Because W&B automatically rejects unverified claims
Because assertions take longer to write than tables
questions.explain: Showing the reported number against yours, the reproduction tier you're claiming, and a link to the actual run and logged config makes the claim checkable, not just stated.

questions.q: A student's extension found no measurable effect. How should this be handled in the write-up, according to this lesson?
options: Omit the extension section entirely to avoid looking unsuccessful
Report it directly and with the same rigor as a positive result, consistent with Lesson 34's approach to negative results
Rerun the experiment until a positive effect appears
Describe it vaguely so the lack of effect isn't obvious
questions.explain: A clearly reasoned null result, with the experiment design shown, is treated as a legitimate and valuable capstone outcome, not something to hide or disguise.

questions.q: What does this lesson recommend a short capstone presentation should lead with?
options: A long narrative of the week-by-week process before any results
The comparison table and evidence, before the process that produced it
A list of every tool used, regardless of relevance
An apology for any limitations before showing any results
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says to lead with the comparison table because the audience wants the evidence first and the journey second.

questions.q: What should a capstone write-up's limitations section plainly state, according to this lesson?
options: Nothing — limitations should be omitted to keep the report confident
Compute budget, seed count, and any setting that may not generalize
A list of unrelated courses the student has completed
Only the limitations of the original paper, not the student's own work
questions.explain: The limitations section is meant to state plainly what the reproduction and extension don't tell you, such as smaller compute, fewer seeds than ideal, or a setting that may not generalize.
